name: Zinnia
grown_as: A half-hardy annual. William's library lists Zinnia marylandica 'Raspberry Lemonade' (the Zahara Raspberry Lemonade mix): a low, disease-resistant hybrid of Z. elegans and Z. angustifolia, 30 to 45 cm, with single flowers in raspberry pink-red, yellow and 'Starlight Rose' (white with a rose band). Drawn in raspberry. ⚠️ CHECK the colour, and whether the drawing should show a mix.
habit: A low, bushy, mounded annual 30 to 45 cm high and as wide, branching from the base, covered in flowers held just above the leaves.

leaf.outline: Lance-shaped to narrow oval, 4 to 8 cm long, narrower than the common zinnia
leaf.base: Stalkless, the base rounded and sitting on or half-clasping the stem
leaf.veins: Three veins from the base, running up beside the midrib

flower.form: A single, flat daisy with one ring of broad rays round a small raised centre
flower.petals: About 10 to 15 broad, flat, oblong ray florets with a small notch or two at the tip; the rays stay on and dry papery as the head ages
flower.colour: Raspberry pink-red (the mix also gives yellow, and white with a rose band at the base)
flower.centre: A small raised dark brown-red disc, ringed with tiny five-pointed yellow star-shaped florets
flower.behind: Rows of rounded, overlapping bracts with dark edges, making a neat cup
flower.carried: Alone at the tips of short branches, facing up, just above the leaves

fruit: The head turns brown with the faded rays still attached and papery. Seeds flat, wedge- to arrowhead-shaped, grey-brown, about 1 cm, packed in a cone.
seedling: Two rounded to oblong, smooth seed leaves on a short stem. The first true leaves come as an opposite pair, lance-shaped and rough.
winter: Nothing: killed by the first frost.

leaf: lance-shaped leaf with no stalk, the base meeting the stem
bloom: one ring of broad flat rays with notched tips
small raised dark centre ringed with tiny yellow stars
rounded overlapping bracts behind making a cup
seed: flat wedge- or arrowhead-shaped grey-brown seed
seedling: first opposite pair of lance-shaped leaves
young: low bushy plant branching from the base
flower: compact mound 30 to 45 cm covered in single flowers
flowers just above the leaves on short stems
seedhead: dried brown head with papery faded rays still attached

look_alikes: Common zinnia (Zinnia elegans) is taller with broader oval leaves and larger, often fully double heads. Zinnia angustifolia has very narrow leaves and small orange flowers. Rudbeckia has alternate hairy leaves and a big dark cone.
